I'll just read them out so everybody is aware of what the recommendations are. That the report be received and noted that Council notes the significant impact on Council's revenue of the New South Wales Government's proposed reforms to the infrastructure contributions of $4.5 million over 15 years. The Council supports—item 3—Council supports the local government, New South Wales and NESROC advocacy efforts, including submissions to the Parliamentary Inquiry into the Environmental Planning and Assessment Amendment Infrastructure Contributions Bill 2021, and four, that Council writes to the Premier, the Honourable Gladys Berejiklian, the Treasurer, the Honourable Dominic Perrottet, the Minister for Planning and Open Space, the Honourable Rob Stokes, the Minister for Local Government, the Honourable Shelby Hancock, Opposition Leader, Mr Chris Minns, and the Local Member of Parliament and Minister for Counterterrorism and Corrections, the Honourable Anthony Roberts. It's to advocate for additional modelling, consultation and mechanisms to ensure contributions are paid in a timely way and that no Council is worse off under the proposals. Now, in relation to this matter, development infrastructure contributions help deliver the infrastructure needed as communities grow and change. They are a means of financing public infrastructure, increased services, provisions, and is required as a direct or indirect result of new dwellings, alterations, additions, knockdown, rebuilds and new non-residential developments, such as office and retail spaces. Council requires contributions from all types of developments to deliver high-quality infrastructure, open space, services and placemaking activities that communities and governments expect. Rate revenue is required to fund ongoing delivery of maintenance of existing services and assets. The implications of this, although the details of the infrastructure contributions reforms are not available, modelling based on the information available indicates significant reductions—significant reduced income for NESROC Councils. This is an issue that's been looked at collectively by our Northern Region Organisation Council. Declines are likely to occur to both the S7-11 contributions and the S7-12 fixed rate levy projected income levels, depending on details, as yet unsighted and not consulted upon. Under the proposed reforms, NESROC Councils face a loss of $171 million in the first five years, $325 million over 10 years and $461 million over 15 years. There is a chart there, and it's clearly unsustainable for local government to take this sort of reduction in its income. The issue is currently before the New South Wales Parliament, has potential to impact on the operations for decades to come. It is critical that all Councils proactively advocate for meaningful modelling, consultation and mechanisms to ensure that Councils are no worse off. Because what the situation is, and it's highlighted in a letter I received from the LORD MAYOR of the City of Sydney, and I'll just read a couple of bits out of that which I think are quite pertinent. I write to you about the shocking changes to the infrastructure contributions that the State Government is trying to rush through Parliament under cover of budget. As you will be aware, the proposed amendments of the Act will radically change the way local infrastructure is planned, funded and delivered. The changes proposed effectively shifting contribution income from Councils into State Government coffers. To compensate Councils for cutting off this revenue stream, the Government has said it will allow us as a Council to charge higher rates. This leaves Council with an impossible choice to stop building and maintaining infrastructure or start charging residents more in rates. Regardless, our community will be worse off. So, this is a quite crucial issue, not only for this Council, but for all Councils across New South Wales. As the Mayoral Minute states, it is a collective response by all the Councils in the Northern Region organisation of Councils to advocate to restore this funding source for local Government, and it is very important for our community as well. So, is there any debate in relation to the matter? Councillor Sandson.
